ai.seo_question: How is the Imām al-Mahdī described in relation to wisdom and his role as a successor to the prophets?
ai.summary: In Shia eschatology, this passage from Nahj al-Balagha characterizes the Hidden Imam as the ultimate inheritor of prophetic wisdom, whose intellectual engagement with 'hikmah' serves as both his spiritual armor and his defining identity. The imagery of him being 'strange' when Islam is strange highlights the concept of *ghurba*, emphasizing his role as the final *Hujjah* (Proof) of God who preserves divine knowledge until the time of reappearance. This portrayal underscores the continuity between the Imams and the Prophets, positioning the Mahdi not merely as a political leader but as the culmination of spiritual and intellectual legacy.
